$description: Vellum design tokens. Two layers: `primitive` holds raw values and nothing else; `semantic` maps primitives to roles and is the only layer components may reference. Which component uses which role is recorded in the CSS itself, and the validator reports it. Dual-mode colors carry their light value in `$value` and their dark value in `$extensions['design.vellum.mode'].dark`, so a plain DTCG resolver yields a valid light theme with no special handling. Dimension and duration values are authored as CSS strings rather than {value,unit} objects: this file is read by humans, by CSS generators, and by language models, and the string form is unambiguous to all three.
name: Vellum
author: Jonathan Hockaday

primitive.$description: Raw values. No roles, no modes, no meaning. Never reference these from a component — go through `semantic`.

color.$description: Ramps are DERIVED, not chosen. Each family walks nine fixed CIELAB L* targets (95, 89, 82, 74, 65, 55, 45, 36, 29) at its own hue angle, taking chroma = min(target, gamut max) with OKLCH targets 0.030, 0.062, 0.098, 0.126, 0.145, 0.138, 0.120, 0.100, 0.082. A step number therefore means the same lightness in EVERY hue, which is what lets contrast be reasoned about without checking each ramp — the same premise as Material 3 tones and USWDS grades. To add a colour the system has never carried: take its hue angle and walk the ladder. No hand-tuning. `neutral` is exempt and documented separately; it is tuned for interface use, not for smooth interpolation.

neutral.$description: The scale is not perceptually even — gaps run from 1.9 to 19.3 L*. It is tuned for interface use, not for smooth interpolation. The 550 and 650 half-steps exist to give text roles a rung that clears WCAG AA; see DECISIONS.md 001.

550.$description: BOUNDARY RUNG. AA on the dark sheet needs text lighter than L* 53.1 (re-derived at the dark-ground lift, task 9 — was L* 51.7 against the pre-lift sheet); this sits at 55.0, the first rung clear of that threshold, with a tighter margin than before. Also fills the largest gap in the scale (500->600 is 18.4 L*). See DECISIONS 002, RC6 addendum.

650.$description: BOUNDARY RUNG. AA on the light sheet needs text darker than L* 49.1; this sits at 46.6, clear of it, where 600 at 48.3 leaves almost no margin. Functional rather than expressive. See DECISIONS 002, RC6 addendum.

blue.$description: A palette and chart ramp with no status behind it. It backed status-blue until DECISIONS 058 retired that role, and stays because ramps ship whole (GRAMMAR §3.4, §5): it is the example of a ramp a project may reach for that names no state (DECISIONS 059).

ground-light.$description: The light ground. Never pure white — pure white is reserved for raised surfaces.

ground-dark.$description: The dark ground. Never pure black.

ground-dark-raised.$description: Dark-mode surface lifted off the ground.

ground-dark-deep.$description: Below the dark ground — recessed cavity only. Re-derived under DECISIONS 011 from the owner's dialled cavity delta (-3.6 L* from the tray, chained through the corrected ladder) rather than restated as a fixed target — see DECISIONS 011. Was `#0C0D0E` (L* 3.59) against the ladder's pre-011 chain; now L* 3.28.

steel.$description: Machined fill for physical control handles. Not a text or surface colour.

action-ink-dark.$description: Dark mode's primary action fill at rest — targets the owner's dialled `act` value of L* 88 (`#DDDDDD` itself computes to L* 88.12) (DECISIONS 011). Deliberately not a neutral-ramp rung: the ramp's greys carry a slight blue cast (GRAMMAR §3.4's chroma targets), and `--color-action-bg` is GRAMMAR §2.5's "monochrome ink" — it must be truly achromatic, not tinted.

action-ink-dark-active.$description: Dark mode's primary action fill under press — L* 79.88, the same -8.2 L* magnitude the system already used for the press gesture (previously 100 -> neutral-300's 91.76) re-based on the new resting L* 88 rather than on pure white. See DECISIONS 011 and GRAMMAR §2.4.

weight.$description: Five steps: 400, 500, 700, 800, 900. There is no 600 (GRAMMAR §2.13, DECISIONS 015). Each step has one role in `semantic.weight`; reach a weight through its role, not the number.

size.$description: Type steps. Fluid steps use clamp() so a single token covers the full viewport range.

title.$description: Section titles (h2). The floor sits above --type-heading's 24px so a title and a card heading never render the same size on a phone; at 24px they tied below ~690px wide (DECISIONS 044).

statement.$description: The alternating solid/ghost banner. Lower floor than display because the banner routinely carries long single words, and a clamp floor that stops shrinking on a narrow screen overflows the page.

hero.$description: The floor matters more than the ceiling. A clamp floor stops the type shrinking while the viewport keeps shrinking, so any floor above ~40px guarantees overflow on a 320px screen for words of ordinary length. 56px overflowed by 93px at 320px before this was lowered.

lamp-a.$description: The blur each lamp's softness is measured from. No rule applies it any more: build.js reads it through semantic.lamp's design.vellum.profile and bakes the blurred falloff into the lamp's gradient stops (DECISIONS 064). Its vw term sets the softness, which holds at every width; the px clamps record where the old filter stopped scaling, and are not applied (DECISIONS 064). It scales with the lamp because lamps are sized in vw, so a fixed px blur would quadruple its relative strength between desktop and mobile and flatten the backlight into a wash.

semantic.$description: Roles. The only layer a component may reference. Every token under `semantic.color`, `semantic.elevation`, and `semantic.lamp` carries both an light mode value ($value) and an dark mode value ($extensions['design.vellum.mode'].dark) — the validator fails the build if either is missing.

bg-canvas.$description: Page ground. Never pure white or pure black.

surface-solid.$description: Opaque surface lifted off the ground, for content that must not be translucent.

surface-sunken.$description: Recessed opaque well holding a canvas, video, or live demo. Reads as cut through the sheet, so it never takes sheet treatment or blur.

surface-document.$description: On-screen fill of a printable document sheet — the paper simulated on a monitor before it crosses to `semantic.print`. Distinct from `surface-solid`: this role tracks mode (the on-screen simulation dims in dark mode) where the print token never does.

text-primary.$description: Headlines, titles, active control labels, key values.

design.vellum.provenance.reason: The previous values failed WCAG AA at the sizes this role is actually used at (10.5px). light mode measured 2.37:1 against the canvas where 4.5:1 is required; dark mode measured 4.14:1. See DECISIONS.md 001 for the measurements and how to revert.
design.vellum.provenance.revert: Point $value at {primitive.color.neutral.500} and the dark mode value at {primitive.color.neutral.600}. Nothing else depends on the half-steps.

text-muted.$description: Monospace labels, units, counters, table headers. The smallest type in the system, so it carries the tightest contrast requirement — 4.5:1, not the 3:1 large-text allowance.

text-ghost.$description: Outline weight of the alternating statement banner. Decorative only — never carries information a reader needs.

text-document.$description: Ink for text sitting on `surface-document` — the on-screen simulation of a paper sheet. Softer than `text-primary`'s pure white in dark mode (F8FAFC, not FFFFFF), matching the way the simulated paper itself is never pure black or pure white against the ground.

text-on-sunken.$description: Primary text on `surface-sunken`. Mode-invariant on purpose: `surface-sunken` is dark in BOTH modes (`#0F172A` light, `#0B0C0D` dark), so a role that tracks mode is wrong here — `text-primary` is `#0F172A` in light, the same value as the cavity, and renders 1.00:1, invisible. Reach for it wherever text sits on any recessed opaque well, not only a stage cavity. Its pairing is declared in `validate_system.js` (GRAMMAR §2.6) and measured in both modes on every build.

text-on-sunken-secondary.$description: Quieter text on `surface-sunken` — captions and labels beneath `text-on-sunken`, the second step of a two-step ladder. Mode-invariant for the same reason: the well is dark in both modes. It is `neutral-500`, the value `text-secondary` takes in dark mode. Named for its step, not for the monospace it happens to be set in. Pairing declared and measured as for `text-on-sunken`.

surface.$description: Outer sheet — the system’s primary surface. Translucency is load-bearing: it must sit over the light table to read correctly. Dark's tint is ground-toned, not black — DESIGN §5.1's reasoning against an opaque-reading white sheet applies symmetrically against black. Alpha derived (not chosen) to composite `ground-dark` down by the owner's dialled 1.1 L* card drop (DECISIONS 011), landing at L* 7.26 against the real ground's measured L* 8.36 — not the 7.40 Task 8 pinned, which chained from a ground reading with a rounding bug. See DECISIONS 008/010/011.

border.$description: The 1px edge of a sheet, where its thickness catches the light. In light mode: always 1px, never coloured. In dark mode: zero — the owner dialled this to 0 and DECISIONS 011 makes GRAMMAR §2.3 mode-aware to match, rather than shipping a non-zero compliance value against a rule that no longer applies to dark's material. See DECISIONS 010 (which first flagged this as provisional) and 011 (which resolves it).

border-hover.$description: Edge of a lifted sheet. In light mode, brighter, never a different hue — the lift catches more light, it does not change colour. In dark mode: zero, per the owner's explicit ruling ("as for the rim, both should be 0") — the resting edge was already 0 (DECISIONS 011); the hover edge, previously kept non-zero as the owner's own separate carve-out, now joins it. See DECISIONS 010's second addendum.

surface-raised.$description: Inner tray nested inside an outer sheet. Denser than surface so the nesting reads. Dark's tray composites over the CARD (`--color-surface`), not over the ground — alpha derived to carry `--color-surface` at L* 7.26 down by the owner's dialled 0.3 L* tray drop to L* 6.96 (DECISIONS 011), ground-toned like the card it nests inside. Was L* 7.10 under Task 8's pre-011 ladder.

design.vellum.provenance.changed: 1.0.0-RC5; dark re-derived at the dark-ground-lift, task 9
design.vellum.provenance.reason: A nav is the only sheet that passes over ARBITRARY content, so it is the only one whose backdrop is unbounded. Every other sheet sits on the known, pale ground. At surface's 0.65 white, nav links measured 3.41:1 over --color-surface-sunken and 3.11:1 over pure black — both below AA. At 0.85 they measure 5.15:1 and 4.95:1. The alpha floor for AA over pure black is 0.785; 0.85 keeps headroom. Ground-coloured rather than white on purpose: a dense sheet approaches the tone of the paper itself, which is what diffusion does. White at this alpha would read as an opaque bar rather than vellum. Dark's RC5 figure was never independently derived — its alpha was assumed symmetric with light's at 0.85, and its rgb literally equalled the OLD ground (#0A0B0E = rgb(10,11,14)). The dark-ground lift (#0A0B0E, L* 3.03 -> #18181B, L* 8.36) broke both assumptions: rgb(10,11,14) is now the wrong ground entirely, and even corrected to the new ground rgb, 0.85 measures only 4.38:1 over pure white — below AA. The recomputed dark floor is alpha 0.858; dark now ships at 0.9 (rgb updated to the new ground, #18181B), measuring 5.20:1 over pure white and 6.99:1 over --color-surface-sunken — headroom in the same spirit as light's. Light is untouched: its ground did not move.
design.vellum.provenance.revert: Point the nav sheet's background back at var(--color-surface) and delete this role (reintroduces DECISIONS 002's failure), or — to revert only the dark re-derivation — point the dark value back at rgba(10, 11, 14, 0.85) (reintroduces the AA failure this note describes, now against the lifted ground).

surface-nav.$description: The nav sheet. Denser than every other surface because it is the only one whose backdrop is unbounded — a page may scroll a black photograph beneath it in light mode, or a white one in dark mode. Density here is a legibility floor, not a style choice: see the provenance note before lowering it.

border-subtle.$description: Underline on a nav sheet. Quieter than border because it runs the full viewport width.

border-document.$description: Edge of a simulated-paper surface (`surface-document`). Shares `border`'s light value. Zero in dark, as every sheet edge is (GRAMMAR §2.3): the document sheet composites 2.94 L* below the dark ground, nearly three times the standard sheet's 1.10, so its luminance step carries it without a line (DECISIONS 025).

action-bg.$description: Primary action fill. Monochrome ink that inverts across modes — an accent hue here is a brand violation. Dark's fill is the owner's dialled grey targeting L* 88 (`#DDDDDD`, L* 88.12) (DECISIONS 011), not pure white as RC10 shipped — it now has headroom above it. See `action-bg-hover`/`action-bg-active` and GRAMMAR §2.4.

action-bg-hover.$description: Primary action fill under the cursor. A solid surface rising toward the light catches more of it, so the fill lightens — but only where the material has headroom. In light mode the ink lifts one ramp step. In dark mode, as of DECISIONS 011, the resting fill targets L* 88 (`#DDDDDD`, L* 88.12), not pure white — pure white is now the CEILING it lifts toward rather than the value it already sits at, so this token is unchanged (still `white`) but the relationship inverts: hover now moves the fill (+12 L*, to the ceiling) instead of holding at it. Never a fade: opacity would drag the label's contrast down with the fill, and would move the two modes in opposite directions.

action-bg-active.$description: Primary action fill while pressed. The mirror of action-bg-hover: pressing re-couples the sheet to the board, so the fill DARKENS by the same magnitude hover lightens — but only where the material has headroom. Light mode holds: its fill is already neutral-900 with just 8.0 L* above pure black, which GRAMMAR 2.5 prohibits as a fill, so the deepened shadow carries the gesture alone. Dark mode, as of DECISIONS 011, drops the same -8.2 L* it always has, now re-based on the dialled L* 88 rest value instead of pure white — landing at L* 79.88 rather than the old neutral-300 (L* 91.76), since neutral-300 was only ever a coincidence of the drop landing on an existing rung when the base was 100.

action-fg.$description: Label on a primary action. The one place pure black is permitted.

action-border.$description: Edge of an unselected control or secondary action, and the slider's track. Set at the opacity that gives 3:1 against the ground and a sheet in each mode, WCAG 1.4.11's minimum for a control's boundary; was 0.12 / 0.15, at 1.31:1 / 1.57:1 (DECISIONS 034).

divider.$description: Structural hairline between rows, columns, and table cells.

rule-strong.$description: A 40% ink hairline — a distinct, heavier role from `divider` (0.06). Used for a short accent rule that must read as a deliberate mark, not a structural seam.

rule-document.$description: Structural hairline beneath a simulated-paper surface's letterhead-style header, echoing the solid printed rule the on-screen document simulates. Solid ink in light mode rather than an alpha wash, unlike `divider` and `rule-strong` — a heavier, more literal line than either, reserved for a document surface's own header rule.

wash-hover.$description: Barely-there tint under a hovered row. Below the threshold of being read as a colour. Dark rides the action dial (DECISIONS 011): the shipped 0.03 x the new act ratio 0.88 (L* 88 / 100).

wash-active.$description: Tint under a selected chip that is not a primary action. Dark rides the action dial (DECISIONS 011): the shipped 0.10 x the new act ratio 0.88 (L* 88 / 100).

wash-subtle.$description: Static-region tint, marking a broad fixed area of a surface as distinct without drawing attention to it — a table header row, a banded section. Named for its intensity, not a state, because a static region has no state to name; not an interaction state like `wash-hover`/`wash-active`. A denser rung, `wash-strong`, was removed unused (DECISIONS 044).

focus-ring.$description: Halo outside the focus border. Monochrome — the browser default blue is prohibited.

control-thumb.$description: Fill of a slider handle. Reads as a machined part, not a UI dot.

control-thumb-ring.$description: Collar separating the handle from its track.

status-red.$description: Failure: down, failed, refused, out. A fixed job. A project may replace the colour only inside red's family, 0–35° or 345–360° (GRAMMAR §3.9, DECISIONS 058). Status only — never a headline, button fill, or decoration.

status-amber.$description: Attention and warning. A fixed job. A project may replace the colour only inside amber's family, 40–95° (GRAMMAR §3.9, DECISIONS 058). Status only — never a headline, button fill, or decoration.

status-emerald.$description: Live, connected, operational. A fixed job. A project may replace the colour only inside emerald's family, 120–170°: a forest green, not a teal (GRAMMAR §3.9, DECISIONS 058). Status only.

status-cyan.$description: A free status: no fixed job. Each project names the state it reports, and may replace the colour with any hue outside the three families and their margins, a brand colour included. Its default sits on brand 4's hue, 215° (GRAMMAR §3.9, DECISIONS 058). Status only.

status-purple.$description: A free status: no fixed job. Each project names the state it reports, and may replace the colour with any hue outside the three families and their margins, a brand colour included. Its default sits on brand 2's hue, 304° (GRAMMAR §3.9, DECISIONS 058). Status only.

status-red-fg.$description: Text on a red status tint. A RUNG, not a chosen colour: 700 in light mode, 500 in dark. The 12% tint composites to L* ~94 in light mode and ~15 in dark mode, so no single value clears AA in both. Across every hue angle the 700 rung clears 4.5:1 on the light tint (worst 4.62:1, at hue 189) and the 500 rung clears it on the dark tint (worst 5.60:1, at hue 300), so a replaced or declared status is legible by construction (DECISIONS 058). Changing the tint percentage invalidates this pairing — see the contrast-pairing check in validate_system.js.

status-amber-fg.$description: Text on a amber status tint. A RUNG, not a chosen colour: 700 in light mode, 500 in dark. The 12% tint composites to L* ~94 in light mode and ~15 in dark mode, so no single value clears AA in both. Across every hue angle the 700 rung clears 4.5:1 on the light tint (worst 4.62:1, at hue 189) and the 500 rung clears it on the dark tint (worst 5.60:1, at hue 300), so a replaced or declared status is legible by construction (DECISIONS 058). Changing the tint percentage invalidates this pairing — see the contrast-pairing check in validate_system.js.

status-emerald-fg.$description: Text on a emerald status tint. A RUNG, not a chosen colour: 700 in light mode, 500 in dark. The 12% tint composites to L* ~94 in light mode and ~15 in dark mode, so no single value clears AA in both. Across every hue angle the 700 rung clears 4.5:1 on the light tint (worst 4.62:1, at hue 189) and the 500 rung clears it on the dark tint (worst 5.60:1, at hue 300), so a replaced or declared status is legible by construction (DECISIONS 058). Changing the tint percentage invalidates this pairing — see the contrast-pairing check in validate_system.js.

status-cyan-fg.$description: Text on a cyan status tint. A RUNG, not a chosen colour: 700 in light mode, 500 in dark. The 12% tint composites to L* ~94 in light mode and ~15 in dark mode, so no single value clears AA in both. Across every hue angle the 700 rung clears 4.5:1 on the light tint (worst 4.62:1, at hue 189) and the 500 rung clears it on the dark tint (worst 5.60:1, at hue 300), so a replaced or declared status is legible by construction (DECISIONS 058). Changing the tint percentage invalidates this pairing — see the contrast-pairing check in validate_system.js.

status-purple-fg.$description: Text on a purple status tint. A RUNG, not a chosen colour: 700 in light mode, 500 in dark. The 12% tint composites to L* ~94 in light mode and ~15 in dark mode, so no single value clears AA in both. Across every hue angle the 700 rung clears 4.5:1 on the light tint (worst 4.62:1, at hue 189) and the 500 rung clears it on the dark tint (worst 5.60:1, at hue 300), so a replaced or declared status is legible by construction (DECISIONS 058). Changing the tint percentage invalidates this pairing — see the contrast-pairing check in validate_system.js.

doc-affirm.$description: DOCUMENTATION CHROME ONLY. Marks a correct example in the style guide. Never appears in a product interface — a page that uses this outside the workbench has mistaken the manual for the system.

doc-negate.$description: DOCUMENTATION CHROME ONLY. Marks a prohibited example in the style guide. Chosen to sit outside the product palette, so it could not be mistaken for a status colour. Since DECISIONS 058 the core has a red status at 25°, and this sits in red's family; it stays documentation chrome only, and whether it moves is open.

accent.$description: One colour for small marks: a status pill, a dot, a rule. It is one of the brand colours, named from the palette, never a hex of its own: brand 1 by default, and a project may point it at any brand colour it declares (DECISIONS 047). The same in both modes: a brand hex does not change with the ground. The brand itself is carried by the lamps, from the palette (semantic.brand, GRAMMAR §3.3, §3.5). The accent stays bound by the status-only rule: it may tint a pill, a dot, or a rule, and may never fill a primary action or colour a headline. The status colours do not move with it (DECISIONS 058). Before DECISIONS 046 this held the same hex as a literal.

stage.$description: Resting sheet. The inset top line is the lit edge and is not optional in light mode. In dark mode, DECISIONS 011 (amending 010): the owner dialled the shadow to 0, not merely stepped back — depth reads entirely by the luminance step between attenuating sheets, with no cast shadow at all. Was `0 12px 32px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.30)` under 010's still-present-but-reduced shadow; that reduction was correct in direction but not in destination.

hover.$description: Lifted sheet. In light mode, deepens the ambient shadow and brightens the lit edge — it never adds colour. In dark mode, per DECISIONS 011 (amending 010): the shadow carries nothing, at rest or lifted — 0 in both `stage` and `hover`. The rim, which briefly carried the read of lift on its own (0 at rest, 0.20 on hover, DECISIONS 010's first addendum), is now 0 on hover too — the owner's later, explicit ruling ("as for the rim, both should be 0") retired the carve-out that had kept it lit. See DECISIONS 010's second addendum.

sm.$description: Resting element that is not a sheet. Zero in dark, like every shadow role: dark has no directional light to cast one (GRAMMAR §2.3, DECISIONS 025).

md.$description: Lifted control: icon button, hovered pill. Zero in dark (GRAMMAR §2.3, DECISIONS 025).

lg.$description: Floating layer: dialog, popover. Zero in dark (GRAMMAR §2.3, DECISIONS 025).

action-hover.$description: Cast by a hovered primary action. Tinted to the ink colour of its own mode, so the button appears to lift off the ground rather than glow.

nav-scrolled.$description: Cast by a persistent nav sheet once it has laid down over scrolled content. A real role the system had never named — distinct from `stage` and `md`, neither of which matches its spread. Zero in dark (GRAMMAR §2.3, DECISIONS 025).

viewport.$description: Cast by a deep-set frame holding presented content at a remove from the page — a deck slide viewer, or any other bounded stage the reader looks INTO rather than at. Sits deeper and wider than `stage`, which is a resting sheet on the page itself, not a frame around separately-presented content. Zero in dark, shadow and inset rim alike (GRAMMAR §2.3, DECISIONS 025).

document-sheet.$description: Cast by the printable spec sheet's on-screen simulation. Distinct from `stage` — the sheet has no lit inset edge, since it reads as paper, not as a translucent surface. Zero in dark (GRAMMAR §2.3, DECISIONS 025).

thumb.$description: Cast by a slider's thumb, a solid knob sitting on its track. The light value is the one `styles.css` had written literally; zero in dark, like every shadow role (GRAMMAR §2.3, DECISIONS 028). A focused thumb adds its ring in front of this.

thumb-active.$description: A slider thumb while it is being dragged. Zero in dark (GRAMMAR §2.3, DECISIONS 028).

brand.$description: THE PROJECT'S PALETTE. A brand brings as many colours as it has; each is declared here exactly as given, never rounded to a rung, and each makes its own nine steps with derive_ramp.js (GRAMMAR §3.3–3.4). The lamps take their colours from this palette, per mode: each lamp is a brand colour, a step of one, or a neutral grey, or it is off (GRAMMAR §3.5). A brand colour is mode-invariant — a hex does not change with the ground — so dark mode chooses different colours rather than redefining these. These five are Vellum's own, read back from the lamps it has always shipped (DECISIONS 046). A project replaces them with its own; numbering is order of declaration, not rank.

1.$description: Sky. Lights lamp A in light mode.

2.$description: Purple. Lights lamp B in light mode.

3.$description: Green. Lights lamp C in light mode. Lamp C is off in dark.

4.$description: Cyan. Lights lamp A in dark mode — a different colour from light's, because light to dark does not always carry over.

5.$description: Deep purple. Lights lamp B in dark mode. The same hue as brand 2, so it makes the same nine steps, but its own hex: deeper and more saturated than any of those steps.

lamp.$description: The light table: up to three soft radial lamps behind all content, painted by .light-table itself as opaque gradient layers that build.js generates from these tokens (DECISIONS 064). They are what a sheet diffuses; remove them and every sheet goes flat. Each lamp is declared per mode by two values: a colour (`a-color`) and the peak opacity it is drawn at (`a-opacity`, 0 to 1). The colour comes from the brand palette (semantic.brand): a brand colour, a step of one, or a neutral grey, and it is opaque, because a translucent colour makes the generated stops translucent again and brings back the banding they exist to remove. A lamp that is off is opacity 0. Which colour lights which lamp is the project's choice, made per mode (GRAMMAR §3.5, DECISIONS 046); the opacity budget is not. Opacity is bounded at BOTH ends per mode (see design.vellum.bounds): below the floor a sheet has nothing left to diffuse, above the ceiling the lamps stop being ambient light and become decoration. The two modes differ because equal alpha is not equal effect - dark mode's dark ground does not compete with the lamp, so it passes more colour per unit. The bounds are matched by EFFECT: dark mode 0.26 puts as much colour through a sheet as light mode 0.45 (30.6 against 30.9), so the ceiling means the same thing in both modes. The floors match the same way: dark mode 0.07 and light mode 0.12 both move a sheet 8.25. The dark mode ceiling is not headroom reserved above the system's own defaults — Task 8's lamp A settled exactly at 0.26, the ceiling itself, once the ground lifted. The ceiling bounds how far any PROJECT may push its own hue past what the system ships, not a promise that the shipped defaults stay clear of it.

design.vellum.profile.$description: What build.js reads to write each lamp's gradient stops; none of it is emitted as a custom property (DECISIONS 064). `size` is each lamp's diameter before --lamp-scale. `blur` names the blur each lamp used to be drawn with: its vw term, times `soft` for the mode, over the lamp's radius, fixes the lamp's softness, and the generator bakes the blurred falloff into 24 stops. Softness is constant at every width, as the owner ruled (DECISIONS 064): only the vw term is read, and the px clamps record where the old filter stopped scaling.

a-color.$description: Lamp A's colour. Top-left in both modes. Brand 1 (sky) in light, brand 4 (cyan) in dark. Emitted as var(--brand-n), never the hex, so a project that repoints the brand colour moves the lamp with it (DECISIONS 046).

a-opacity.$description: Lamp A's peak opacity, 0 to 1. Light 0.45, the light ceiling; dark settled at 0.26, the ceiling of the dark 0.07–0.26 band (DECISIONS 008).

b-color.$description: Lamp B's colour. Brand 2 (purple) in light, brand 5 (deep purple) in dark. Top-right in light; bottom-right in dark (DECISIONS 008 — dark's distribution is diagonal opposition to A, not a repeat of light's arrangement).

b-opacity.$description: Lamp B's peak opacity, 0 to 1. Light 0.25; dark settled at 0.2275, within the 0.07–0.26 band.

c-color.$description: Lamp C's colour. Brand 3 (green). Mid-centre in light; off in dark, where it keeps light's colour so a project that lights it in dark only has to set the opacity.

c-opacity.$description: Lamp C's peak opacity, 0 to 1. Light 0.2; OFF in dark. DECISIONS 008 permits two lamps in dark — three co-located hues on the dark ground read as a patchwork rather than a field. Its dark opacity is exactly 0, which is exempt from §3.5's dark floor of 0.07 (rules 4j and 4p in validate_system.js): the floor governs a lamp that is present, and a lamp at opacity 0 is an unused slot, not a dim lamp. The layer is still painted, as the canvas colour, which changes nothing under either blend mode.

a-top.$description: Lamp A, pinned from the top edge — percentage of the container's height, per the CSS box model. Reproduces the shipped top-left edge-pin exactly in light. Dark repoints to the owner's dialled centre (5%, 14%) under DECISIONS 011: expressed as a pure-percentage edge pin, never `calc(% - vw)` (the mixed-unit form Task 6 reverted). `top` is a percentage of the container's HEIGHT while the lamp's own box (55vw) is sized from the viewport's WIDTH, so converting a centre to an edge pin is close (not exact — see `a-left`) for `left`/`right`, both terms nominally scaling with width, but calibrated only at one aspect ratio for `top` — here 1512x950, where -29.8% centres the box at 14% of height. It will drift at other aspect ratios, the same inherent limitation Task 8 documented for lamp B.

a-left.$description: Lamp A, pinned from the left edge — percentage of the container's width. Reproduces the shipped top-left edge-pin exactly in light. Dark repoints to the owner's dialled centre (5%, 14%) under DECISIONS 011: -22.5% = centreX (5%) minus half the box's own width (55vw / 2 = 27.5%), both terms expressed as a percentage of viewport width — close, not exact: `.light-table` is `position: fixed`, so its `%` is measured against the viewport width excluding a classic scrollbar, while `vw` includes it. Drift is sub-1% and invisible at these blur radii.

b-top.$description: Lamp B, pinned from the top edge — percentage of the container's height. Light reproduces the shipped top-right edge-pin exactly. Dark repoints to the owner's dialled centre (90%, 92%) under DECISIONS 011, replacing Task 8's 45% (which was calibrated to an earlier, approximate placement, not this centre). Same top-vs-width caveat as lamp A's `a-top`: exact at 1512x950 (yields 92% of height there), calibrated rather than universal, since the lamp's box is sized from viewport width but `top` reads as a percentage of viewport height.

b-right.$description: Lamp B, pinned from the right edge — percentage of the container's width. Lamp B pins by `right` while A and C pin by `left`; that asymmetry is the system's own shape, not tidied away. Reproduces the shipped top-right edge-pin exactly in light. Dark repoints under DECISIONS 011: -15% = 100% - centreX (90%) - half the box's own width (50vw / 2 = 25%), both terms in percentage of viewport width — close, not exact: `.light-table` is `position: fixed`, so its `%` is measured against the viewport width excluding a classic scrollbar, while `vw` includes it. Drift is sub-1% and invisible at these blur radii.

c-top.$description: Lamp C, pinned from the top edge — percentage of the container's height. Reproduces the shipped mid-centre edge-pin exactly. Dark repeats light — lamp C is off in dark (opacity 0, DECISIONS 008), so its position is inert there.

c-left.$description: Lamp C, pinned from the left edge — percentage of the container's width. Reproduces the shipped mid-centre edge-pin exactly. Dark repeats light — lamp C is off in dark (opacity 0, DECISIONS 008), so its position is inert there.

scale.$description: Multiplier on each lamp's own diameter (the profile's `size`: 55vw/50vw/45vw). Light holds at 1. Dark's 0.98 is the owner's dialled `lsize` (DECISIONS 011), applied in the generated .light-table layers as `calc(27.5vw * var(--lamp-scale) * reach)` rather than as per-mode literals, since a per-mode literal would silently un-apply in light. The generator also reads it, per mode, to fix each lamp's softness ratio, so a project that changes it resizes a lamp without changing how soft its edge is in proportion (DECISIONS 064). A 2% diameter change is small — see DECISIONS 011 for whether it registers on screen.

display.$description: Headlines and stat numerals. Weight 800–900 only.

mono.$description: Every mechanical label, badge, counter, unit, and CTA. Uppercase, except code, identifiers and units, which keep their literal case (GRAMMAR §2.1, DECISIONS 030).

headline.$description: Headlines, the top of the ladder: h1, the hero, the statement banner and stat numerals (GRAMMAR §2.13).

title.$description: Section heads and every subhead set in the display face: h3–h6 and card titles. Display type never drops below it (GRAMMAR §2.1, §2.13).

bold.$description: The emphasis weight and the workhorse: labels, table headers, spec keys, eyebrows, and the selected half of every 500/700 pair (GRAMMAR §2.13).

medium.$description: The resting state of an interactive label whose selected state is --weight-bold: a sidebar row not yet chosen, an accordion question that is closed. A state, not a lighter emphasis. Where a weight must read lighter than 700, it is this one; 600 is not a step (GRAMMAR §2.13, DECISIONS 015).

body.$description: Running prose. Inherited, so it is rarely declared (GRAMMAR §2.13).

display.$description: The tightest display step, for the largest type: h1, the hero, and large stat numerals. Display tracking tightens with size and is never positive: statement banners, slide titles and headings set larger than a section title take --tracking-statement; section and card titles, subheads and wordmarks take --tracking-title. Display type is nearly always set in capitals, and capitals need more room than mixed case, so this was loosened from -0.055em (GRAMMAR §2.1, DECISIONS 029, 061).

statement.$description: Statement banners, slide titles, and display headings set larger than a section title (--type-title). Was -0.04em (DECISIONS 061). Large stat numerals moved to --tracking-display (DECISIONS 062).

title.$description: Section and card titles, subheads, and wordmarks: display type at --type-title or smaller. Zero, because capitals at these sizes crowd when tightened. Was -0.02em (DECISIONS 061).

mono.$description: Monospace inside a control: buttons, pills, inline labels.

mono-wide.$description: Monospace standing alone as a section eyebrow or kicker. Wider because it has no enclosing border to give it structure.

type.$description: One scale for the whole system. A medium (deck, print) may scale it, but may not invent steps.

body.$description: Running prose. The system's base size.

small.$description: Captions, dense table cells, button labels.

micro.$description: Chips and table headers. The floor for anything a reader READS. Dense controls at the compact breakpoints compress below it — down to 9.5px on chips at or below 420px — because a control label is scanned rather than read, and the target it sits in is what has to stay usable. That compression is capped at the console family and must not spread to content type; GRAMMAR §5 states it and check 4v holds it (DECISIONS 026). Contrast does not relax with it: WCAG gives no size allowance until 18.66px, so these carry the same 4.5:1 as everything else.

display.$description: Hero and display type, set flush: large lines sit closer than their size suggests.

loose.$description: Lists set in small type, where each item needs air: .spec-list.

radius.$description: Radius encodes what a thing IS, not how big it is. A pill is always fully round; a machined control is always 6px. Choosing a radius by taste breaks the grammar.

stage.$description: Outer sheet: the stage, a card, the telemetry bar. Since DECISIONS 048 the only 20px role.

tray.$description: Inner tray nested inside a sheet. Named for what it IS, as the whole radius family is - radius encodes identity (GRAMMAR 2.8). The blur family is named for DEPTH instead, which is why the same component is --blur-raised there.

control.$description: Machined control: mode button, stepper, input.

blur.$description: Blur depth encodes elevation. Deeper blur = further from the reader. The ladder is fixed: stage 40 > drawer 30 > nav 24 > raised 20 > field 10.

smooth.$description: Header reveal, drawer expand, and layout changes such as the workbench frame resizing. The one 350ms role (DECISIONS 049).

slow.$description: The slowest step, for ambient motion that repeats: the live status dot's pulse (DECISIONS 051).

spring.$description: The system's only easing curve. Decelerating, no overshoot.

compact.$description: The console family's compact width. Inside a max-width query at or below it, compact controls may set labels down to 9.5px; nothing else goes below --type-micro (GRAMMAR §5, DECISIONS 026).

mobile.$description: Data tables collapse to card stacks at or below this width.

tablet.$description: Narrow layout: nav links fold away, side-by-side panels drop to one or two columns, and padding tightens.

desktop.$description: Multi-column grids collapse at or below this width.

print.$description: Paper medium. Deliberately mode-invariant: a sheet has no dark mode, so these must never be redeclared under [data-theme]. Process inks only — no translucency, no blur, no shadow can survive the crossing.

ink.$description: 100% K, pure black. All text on paper. The screen's slate text (#0F172A) is not carried across: print repoints the text roles to these inks (DECISIONS 045).

ink-secondary.$description: 60% K, a neutral grey with no blue in it. Subtitles, metadata rails, and any text the screen sets in a secondary or muted role.

rule.$description: Structural hairline, 100% K. 0.5pt at final size.

rule-light.$description: Interior table rule. A neutral grey at the lightness of the slate it replaced (L* 91.8), so paper carries no blue (DECISIONS 045).

fill.$description: Table header tint. The only fill permitted on paper. Neutral, at the lightness of the slate it replaced (L* 96.2).

deck.$description: 16:9 slide medium. Scales the shared type scale for projection distance; adds no new roles and no new colours.
